child_handoff_protocol.slot_precondition: fds 198 and 199 are closed in the parent before setup; any pre-existing descriptor fails before invocation publication
child_handoff_protocol.parent_setup: open and exclusively flock the runtime lock, create an O_CLOEXEC pipe, dup2 runtime lock to fd 198 inheritable and pipe write end to fd 199 inheritable, keep the ACK read end private
child_handoff_protocol.popen: start_new_session=true, close_fds=true, pass_fds=(198,199), exact child argv includes --runtime-lock-fd 198 --handoff-ack-fd 199
child_handoff_protocol.parent_close_order: immediately after successful Popen close the parent's original runtime-lock fd, original pipe write fd and local fd 199; retain only local fd 198 until handoff acceptance or until a failed child is reaped; on Popen error close every original and fixed-slot descriptor before publishing the POPEN_ERROR exit receipt
child_handoff_protocol.child_order: validate fd 198 is the exact regular runtime-lock path and owns the inherited flock; validate fd 199 is writable; write exactly one byte 0x41; close fd 199; perform all child work; fsync every child-owned output; close fd 198 only as the final child-owned action before process return
child_handoff_protocol.ack_validation: parent uses monotonic poll with 5000ms deadline and reads at most two bytes; accepted sequence is exactly 0x41 followed by EOF; EOF before 0x41, any different byte, any second byte or timeout is handoff failure
child_handoff_protocol.handoff_failure: send SIGTERM to the child process group, wait 1000ms, send SIGKILL if still alive, waitpid exactly once, publish exit receipt with handoff_status EOF_BEFORE_ACK, MALFORMED_ACK, EXTRA_ACK or TIMEOUT
child_handoff_protocol.parent_after_ack: close local fd 198 only after exact ACK acceptance; the child inherited descriptor continues to hold the flock
child_handoff_protocol.recovery: after acquiring orchestrator lock, block until fd 198 runtime flock is acquirable; this proves the child completed all child-owned writes or never launched
